title: Which pieces should a new clothing brand sample first?
seoTitle: Planning Your First Clothing Collection for Sampling
description: Choose a lead style, decide which ideas can share development work and turn a first collection concept into a manageable sampling plan.
author: BEWE4R team
intro: Choose the first sample by asking what you most need to learn before the launch. If your brand depends on an unusual fit, start with the garment that proves the fit. If your audience already recognises your illustration, test how it looks on the intended fabric. You can then decide which other pieces are ready to move forward.

toc.text: Separate a garment question from a material question
Which sample should a small label commission first?
Make a decision after the fitting

bodyHtml:
Give each style a job

Picture a first collection with a boxy tee, a cropped hoodie and a matching jogger. The hoodie carries the brand’s distinctive shape. The tee carries its illustration. The jogger only makes sense if customers can wear it with the hoodie. Sampling every colour of all three at once would leave the team reviewing several different problems at the same time.

Write a one-sentence reason for each piece. If two styles do the same job, consider whether both need to enter the first round. Keep the other concept in the collection plan, along with the decision that would make you bring it back.

Separate a garment question from a material question

  • To find out where the hoodie hem sits, fit a garment sample in material representative of the intended bulk.
  • To see whether the small lettering fills in, request a print or embroidery trial at actual size on the intended ground.
  • To review two colours together, start with identified swatches before commissioning another full garment for that decision.
  • To see if two pieces work as a set, schedule a fitting when both samples can be worn together.

What can share an approval?

The same logo file can help two garments look related. Its application still needs checking if the scale, material or placement changes. A chest graphic on a flat tee and the same design crossing a zipped pocket are two production decisions. Mark approvals as applying to a named style, colour and version so your team knows exactly what can be reused.

Which sample should a small label commission first?

Choose the piece that answers the biggest open question for the rest of the collection. If your two tops share a new neckline, sample the one that depends most on its shape. If a second piece uses a different material and fit, list those as separate decisions. One successful sample can settle a design direction while leaving another garment’s fit open.

Make a decision after the fitting

Keep a short sheet with three headings: keep for launch, revise and hold. Under each style, write the observation behind the decision. “The waistband rolls when the wearer sits” gives the pattern maker a useful problem. “The set feels off” leaves them guessing. Pick one person to return the combined feedback.

BEWE4R’s first-order checklist covers the information to gather for the initial enquiry. Once you have chosen your lead style, send the drawings or reference photos and name the decision you want the sample to settle.
